description: Attach a resource to an app: a named set of environment variables, such as a database's connection string, that the app reads as secrets. Name the resource. When the organization has none by that name, pass a provider from list_catalog_resources and the first call creates it, returning at once with state provisioning. Call again with the same arguments, env_prefix included, until the state is attached: the call that finds the resource ready attaches it and sets its variables, then asks for a restart if the app is running. The state is attaching while Valet still owes the restart or the variables, and conflicted when a name the resource sets is already set on the app; the answer gives the reason. An existing resource attaches by name alone, including one another app holds. The call is safe to repeat: one name is one resource, and an app can hold several. Pass env_prefix when two resources would set the same variables. Pass plain_vars for plain configuration the app needs beside the database, name to value, readable from the dashboard and never a secret. For a secret, such as an API key, pass its name in secret_names and say in reason why it is needed: the call that attaches also returns a request whose url the person opens, signed in to Valet, to enter each value; follow it with get_request, and never ask the person to type a secret into this conversation. plain_vars and secret_names apply only on the call that attaches, never while the resource provisions or once it is attached, so repeat them on every call. Read the names an attachment sets from list_catalog_resources before writing the app's code. A new database is empty, so the app creates its own tables, and its URL carries the TLS settings it needs. Publish the app first. The running process does not see the variables until the restart completes; get_service shows the attachment's status and when the new process is running. Provisioning takes about a minute; call again every ten seconds. Values are never returned here. Requires connecting a Valet account.

env_prefix.description: Set the resource's variables under PREFIX_NAME rather than NAME, so two resources that set the same variables can both attach. Omit to use the names as they are. Repeat it on every call for one resource: it applies on the call that attaches.

org_name.description: The Valet organization the app belongs to. Omit to use the organization the account joined first.

plain_vars.description: Plain configuration to set in the restart the attach requests, as variable name to value, such as LOG_LEVEL to debug. Readable from the dashboard: never a secret. Set on the call that attaches. Leave out the names the resource sets.

plan.description: The provider's plan. Omit to use its first plan. Repeat it on every call for one resource.

provider.description: The provider to create the resource from, from list_catalog_resources. Required when the organization has no resource by this name.

reason.description: Required with secret_names. One plain sentence, shown to the person on the request page, saying why the value is needed, such as: The app charges cards and needs your Stripe key. At most 280 characters.

resource.description: Required. The resource's name in the organization, such as shop-db: 3 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. Repeat it on every call for one resource.

secret_names.description: Names of secret variables, such as STRIPE_KEY, for the person to enter on the request page. Never values. Requested on the call that attaches. Leave out the names the resource sets.

name: attach_resource
title: Attach a resource to an app
